Ladder arms for the WiZ batten

Allwin's sketch, drawn to scale with the stock he has. Two identical arms, about 70 cm apart, each a ladder of two 42 cm strips with dowel rungs, braced by 32 cm strips, with printed parts at the wall and tip.

Compact arm, v4 parts

No dowels. The beam is two 42 cm strips held 6.4 mm apart by two M4 nuts on each bolt, with the 32 cm ties bolted outside it. The wall plate gets a thin fin in the beam's gap (lower pivot, still slotted ±5 mm for levelling) and a 21 mm block between the ties (upper pivot). The tip hanger is one fin in the gap at the 41 cm holes. Every pivot is clamped between strips, so there's no designed-in play. Faint blue shows the strips.

  • Strength, by hand: the top band carries each tie's 9 N across 13 mm to its screw, about 0.6 MPa. Each hanger arm carries about 2 N over 50 mm, about 0.6 MPa. Typical PLA is good for about 50 MPa. calculated
  • Bolts: M4 × 30 for the lower fin, the tip fin and the 11 and 21 cm beam holes. M4 × 45 at the upper block and the 31 cm tie joint. M4 × 25 for the crossbar.
  • Spacers: two M4 nuts on each beam bolt, between the strips, at 11, 21 and 31 cm.
  • Fit: tighten every pivot until the joint holds by friction. Tighten the tip fin last, once the hanger hangs plumb.
  • Wobble to check: the pivots now sit about 30 mm apart instead of 100, so loose bolts show up as sway at the batten ends. Clamped tight, it should be fine.

Wall plate v3, organic

v3: reshaped by a coarse 3D topology run. The ties' pull goes across a top band (with an arched rib behind the top screw) into the top screw. The rails press the lower ears into the wall through two pads. Two slim legs join them, and a thin bar carries the lower screw. The middle of v2's solid back plate and its bottom centre carried almost nothing, so v3 opens a window and a notch there. Ears, nut pockets, the slot and the countersinks are unchanged from v2. Volume drops from 162 to 104 cm³. v2 is still in the toggle.

Strength, by hand: each tie pulls about 9 N, bending the 8 mm top band over about 47 mm to the top screw. That's about 1 MPa before the rib helps, against roughly 50 MPa for typical PLA. Every member is at least 5 mm. calculated

The single lifted arm's wall plate, modelled in build123d. The ties pivot on the upper ears and the rails on the lower ears. Every joint is an M4 bolt through the strip's existing hole. Faint blue shows where the strips sit.

  • Print: flat on its back, wall face on the bed, no supports. PLA, 0.2 mm layers, 4 walls, 30% gyroid.
  • Hardware: 4 × M4 × 20 bolts, 4 nuts, 4 washers (under the bolt heads). 2 × 4 mm wall screws, 40 mm or longer, with plugs.
  • Fit: 0.5 mm play at each strip face. If a joint rattles, add a washer.
  • Loads: batten 400 g. About 20 N in the ties and about 15 N pulling on the top wall screw. calculated
  • Drop each nut into its pocket, then drive the bolt in from outside through the strip. The pocket holds the nut, so you only need a screwdriver.

Tip hanger v3, organic

From Allwin's sketch, reshaped by a topology run. The run showed the batten's weight goes almost straight from the crossbar bolts up the legs to the pivots. The slab between the bolts only ties the two sides together against a sideways knock. So v3 keeps two curved legs and one arched tie, every member at least 6 mm. A truss with open cells didn't fit: the rails leave only 24 mm of height, and at a 6 mm floor the cells closed up. v2, the solid block, is still in the toggle and prints fine.

PLA is good for tens of MPa, so stress isn't the limit. The 6 mm floor on member width is about print quality and knocks. Bolt-pad movement comes out under 1 µm for the batten's weight and about 2 µm for a sideways knock.

  • Print: on its side, with the flat face holding the whole profile on the bed and no supports. PLA, 0.2 mm layers, 4 walls, 30% gyroid. Every hole has a 45° roof toward the top.
  • Pivots: one M4 × 20 per side, head inside the rails, nut in the hex pocket on each tab's outer face.
  • Crossbar: 2 × M4 × 25 up through the 32 cm strip's 11 and 21 cm holes. The nut slots open on the top face as printed, so drop the nuts in from there.
  • Cable: it rises from the batten centre beside the crossbar, through the open span above the arch. There's no slot to thread.
  • Fit: snug both pivot bolts, let the hanger settle plumb, then tighten until it holds.

Variants: brace on existing holes

Same wall plate pivots (120 mm apart) and the same 300 mm brace. The only change is which rail hole the brace bolts to, and that sets the rail angle. In every version the tip block's underside stays level, so the batten always hangs flat.

A · Levelnew hole at 28.5 cm

Rail level, batten centre about 40 cm out. Matches your sketch. Costs one drilled hole per rail.

B · Tilts downexisting hole 31

No drilling. The tip block is printed as an 11.5° wedge to keep the clip level, and the batten sits about 9 cm lower than in A.

C · Tilts upexisting hole 21

No drilling, but the rail climbs steeply and the batten ends up about 28 cm out and 26 cm higher than in A. It reads as a crane, not a shelf. I'd skip this one.

B flipped · Tilts upexisting hole 31

B mounted upside down. The rail rises 11.5° from the lower pivot and the brace becomes a tie from the upper pivot, pulling instead of pushing. Same parts, no drilling, batten about 5 cm lower than in A.

Stock check: you said you have 4–5 of each strip and dowel, so this takes 4 + 4 strips and 4 dowels. The tip block does the job of your third (tip) rung, which keeps the dowel count inside your stock. 12 cm strips aren't needed.

Notes

  • The brace meets the rail at 275 mm out and 120 mm down, which sets one new hole per rail. No existing hole works without making the plate taller than the printer bed. calculated
  • Between the rails, the ladder doubles as the cable tray. The cable comes off the batten centre, runs along the batten top to one arm, goes up through the tip block, lies on the rungs back to the plate and leaves through a notch toward the outlet.
  • Batten clip: about 50 mm long, centre hole about 4 mm. Both are approximate, read from the product image. approx
  • Arms about 70 cm apart, leaving about 20 cm of batten overhang at each end.
  • Batten weight unknown. With a light batten, deflection at this reach is about 1 mm. assumed load
